title: Design Patterns
subtitle: GoF, concurrency, enterprise and resilience patterns in modern Java

categories.title: Structural
categories.summary: How objects are composed into larger structures.

categories.title: Behavioral
categories.summary: How objects share responsibility and communicate.

categories.title: Enterprise & Architecture
categories.summary: Structuring applications and their data access.

categories.title: Resilience & Cloud
categories.summary: Keeping distributed systems working when parts fail.

items.title: Single Responsibility
items.intent: Give each class one reason to change.

items.title: Open/Closed
items.intent: Extend behavior by adding code, not by editing working code.

items.title: Liskov Substitution
items.intent: A subtype must be usable anywhere its supertype is, without surprises.

items.title: Interface Segregation
items.intent: Prefer several small, focused interfaces to one fat one.

items.title: Dependency Inversion
items.intent: Depend on abstractions; let low-level details implement what high-level code needs.

items.title: Composition over Inheritance
items.intent: Reuse behavior by holding collaborators, not by extending classes.

items.title: Program to an Interface
items.intent: Depend on what a type can do, not on the concrete class that does it.

items.title: Tell, Don't Ask
items.intent: Tell objects what to do instead of pulling out their state to decide for them.

items.title: Factory Method
items.intent: Let a method, overridable or injectable, decide which concrete class to create.

items.title: Abstract Factory
items.intent: Create whole families of related objects without naming their concrete classes.

items.title: Builder
items.intent: Assemble a complex object step by step and validate it when built.

items.title: Prototype
items.intent: Create new objects by copying an existing one.

items.title: Singleton
items.intent: Guarantee one instance per scope; today usually an enum or a DI-managed singleton.

items.title: Adapter
items.intent: Make an incompatible interface look like the one your code expects.

items.title: Bridge
items.intent: Split an abstraction from its implementation so each can vary on its own.

items.title: Composite
items.intent: Treat single objects and groups of objects through one interface.

items.title: Decorator
items.intent: Add behavior to an object by wrapping it in another object with the same interface.

items.title: Facade
items.intent: Offer one simple entry point to a complex subsystem.

items.title: Flyweight
items.intent: Share immutable state between many objects to save memory.

items.title: Proxy
items.intent: Stand in for another object to control access, defer work, or add checks.

items.title: Chain of Responsibility
items.intent: Pass a request along a chain of handlers until one deals with it.

items.title: Command
items.intent: Wrap a request in an object so it can be queued, logged, retried or undone.

items.title: Interpreter
items.intent: Represent a small language as a grammar of classes and evaluate sentences in it.

items.title: Iterator
items.intent: Walk a collection without exposing how it is stored.

items.title: Mediator
items.intent: Centralize how a group of objects talk to each other.

items.title: Memento
items.intent: Capture an object's state so it can be restored later without breaking encapsulation.

items.title: Observer
items.intent: Notify any number of dependents when an object changes.

items.title: State
items.intent: Let an object change its behavior when its internal state changes.

items.title: Strategy
items.intent: Swap one algorithm for another behind a single interface.

items.title: Template Method
items.intent: Fix the skeleton of an algorithm in a base class and let subclasses fill in the steps.

items.title: Visitor
items.intent: Add new operations to a class hierarchy without changing the classes.

items.title: Immutable Object
items.intent: Share state safely between threads by never changing it.

items.title: Guarded Suspension
items.intent: Make a thread wait until a condition holds before it proceeds.

items.title: Producer-Consumer
items.intent: Decouple threads that make work from threads that do it with a queue.

items.title: Thread Pool
items.intent: Reuse a fixed set of worker threads for many short tasks.

items.title: Future / Promise
items.intent: Represent a result that is not ready yet and compose what happens when it is.

items.title: Read-Write Lock
items.intent: Allow many concurrent readers but only one writer.

items.title: Double-Checked Locking
items.intent: Avoid locking on every access to a lazily created object; mostly obsolete today.

items.title: Active Object
items.intent: Give an object its own thread and queue so callers invoke it asynchronously.

items.title: Reactor
items.intent: Handle many I/O sources on few threads by dispatching ready events to handlers.

items.title: Fork-Join
items.intent: Split a task into subtasks, run them in parallel, and combine the results.

items.title: Layered Architecture
items.intent: Organize code into layers where each only talks to the layer below.

items.title: Hexagonal Architecture
items.intent: Keep the domain in the center and plug the outside world in through ports and adapters.

items.title: Model-View-Controller
items.intent: Separate data, presentation and input handling into three roles.

items.title: Model-View-ViewModel
items.intent: Bind a view to a view model that exposes state and commands, free of UI classes.

items.title: Dependency Injection
items.intent: Hand an object its collaborators instead of letting it create or look them up.

items.title: Service Locator
items.intent: Look up services from a global registry; the pattern DI exists to replace.

items.title: Repository
items.intent: Hide storage behind a collection-like interface for domain objects.

items.title: Unit of Work
items.intent: Track changes during a business transaction and commit them together.

items.title: Data Mapper
items.intent: Move data between objects and a database while keeping them ignorant of each other.

items.title: Active Record
items.intent: An object wraps a database row and knows how to save and load itself.

items.title: Specification
items.intent: Express a business rule as a small object that can be combined and reused.

items.title: Data Transfer Object
items.intent: Carry data across a boundary in a plain object shaped for that boundary.

items.title: Domain Event
items.intent: Record that something meaningful happened in the domain so other parts can react.

items.title: CQRS
items.intent: Use separate models for changing state and for reading it.

items.title: Event Sourcing
items.intent: Store the sequence of events that happened and derive current state from them.

items.title: Timeout
items.intent: Bound how long you wait for a call so a slow dependency cannot hold you hostage.

items.title: Retry with Backoff
items.intent: Retry transient failures with growing, randomized delays.

items.title: Circuit Breaker
items.intent: Stop calling a failing dependency for a while and fail fast or fall back.

items.title: Bulkhead
items.intent: Isolate resources per consumer so one failure cannot sink everything.

items.title: Rate Limiter
items.intent: Cap how many requests are accepted per unit of time.

items.title: Idempotent Consumer
items.intent: Make processing a message twice have the same effect as once.

items.title: Transactional Outbox
items.intent: Write the message in the same transaction as the data, then publish it reliably.

items.title: Saga
items.intent: Coordinate a multi-service workflow with local transactions and compensations.

items.title: Cache-Aside
items.intent: Load data into a cache on demand and keep the database as the source of truth.

items.title: Competing Consumers
items.intent: Let several consumers pull from one queue to scale throughput.

items.title: API Gateway
items.intent: Offer clients one entry point that routes, aggregates and secures calls to services.

items.title: Sidecar
items.intent: Run a helper process next to a service to provide cross-cutting capabilities.

items.title: Ambassador
items.intent: Put a helper next to a client to handle its outbound calls.

items.title: Strangler Fig
items.intent: Replace a legacy system piece by piece behind a routing facade.
